description.narrative: • The humanitarian situation in Vietnam is evolving as heavy rains are heading to Northern Central provinces of Quang Tri, Ha Tinh,Nghe An as typhoon Kalmaegi (storm No. 13 to Vietnam) is approaching. We build on our stand-by humanitarian partnership with Da Nang Red Cross to kick-off quickly an emergency response focusing on Da Nang city and or Hue city. This partnership model reflects Oxfam’s global commitment to localisation, working through existing relationships with the People’s Aid Coordinating Committee (PACCOM),the Vietnam Dykes and Disaster Management Authority (VDDMA), and the provincial Red Cross. The targets of this project is in order to: - Meet the emergency relief needs for approximately 1,500 households affected by Typhoon No. 12 and Typhoon No. 13 (approximately 6,576 people) in three communes: Dai Loc, Duy Xuyen, and Nong Son, Da Nang City, over a period of six months, from December 2025 to May 31, 2026. - Meet the needs for improved access to clean water, sanitation, and livelihood restoration for people in the three aforementioned communes. - Enhance awareness and response capabilities among the people and local authorities regarding disaster prevention and mitigation in the context of increasingly unpredictable climate change andthe increasing intensity and frequency of extreme weather events. • Oxfam is monitoring the on-going development of humanitarian context caused by the on-going Vietnam Central Flooding to identify needs and gaps and explore any potential funding opportunities to support the most vulnerable, affected groups inthe worst affected locations including Da Nang and Hue cities, including: - Shelter and essential items - Water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) - Food and livelihoods - Medical care and psychosocial support - Education: restoring educational facilities

participating-org.narrative: In Vietnam , Oxfam is one of the leading international, non -governmental organisation. Since 1955, Oxfam is active in Vietnam withhumanitarian interventions and started development work in the late 1980's. Today, Oxfam works in 26 provinces with people, governments and civil society to promote equality and well-being through social and economic change.
